claim: decide_over_cover returns cancel_group for the strays even when the kept group's stop quantity is smaller than the position, and its reason says the cancel 'loses nothing'.
evidence: python3 crafted input: position_qty=29 long, declared_stop 6.31207143 / target 7.141302, tick 0.0005; legs keep: STP 20 @6.312 + LMT 20 @7.1415, stray: STP 29 @6.2625 + LMT 29 @7.5 -> output `CASE1b cancel_group keep ['keep'] cancel ['stray'] stop_qty 49.0 keeper_stop_qty 20.0 vs position 29`. src/runtime/over_cover_decision.py:218 (stop_qty sum), :339-426 (keeper chosen on PRICE only; no qty test). Consumer scripts/ops/over_cover_proposal.py:154 builds the operator's cancel-ib-order issue body from it and has no qty check either (grep qty/keep in lines 130-230).
expected: Refuse (or a distinct state) unless the kept group's stop qty >= position qty.
actual: Proposes cancelling the full-size stray; executing it leaves 9 of 29 lots with no stop.
population: Pure function, 1 crafted input reproducing it; live call path = over_cover_proposal.py (proposal -> operator fires cancel-ib-order).
detector: New test in tests/test_over_cover_decision.py asserting the under-sized-keeper input refuses.
proposed_fix: After choosing keep, require groups[keep].stop_qty >= qty (else ambiguous_no_action with reason); add the test.

claim: decide_over_cover counts a stop leg whose total_quantity is unreadable as 0, so a keeper of unknown size is kept and every sized group cancelled, and an unreadable leg can also turn a real over-cover into no_over_cover.
evidence: src/runtime/over_cover_decision.py:203 `entry["stop_qty"] += _f(leg.get("total_quantity")) or 0.0`. Crafted: position 29; group a STP qty=None @6.312 (journal), b STP 29 @6.2625, c STP 29 @6.2 -> `CASE2 cancel_group 58.0 ['b', 'c']`. Contradicts the module's own _leg_side docstring rule that an unclassifiable leg is 'never silently dropped from the coverage sum'.
actual: Counted as 0; cancel of both sized groups proposed.
detector: Test: a stop leg with total_quantity None yields not_graded.
proposed_fix: Track unreadable-qty stop legs like unreadable-side legs and return not_graded.

claim: plan_stray_cancels classifies every non-keyed group on the symbol as this trade's stray, including a SIBLING trade's native IB entry bracket (parentId children, IB auto-OCA named by the parent permId), so a keyed re-arm of trade A can cancel trade B's only protection.
evidence: Crafted: plan_stray_cancels([keyed t7001 STP, '990000001' STP parent_id=990000000, '990000001' LMT], 'oca-protect-t7001', side) -> `cancel order_ids: [2, 3] stray ['990000001']`. Entry brackets are parentId children with no ocaGroup set by us (src/units/accounts/ib_client.py:1680-1697). Live /api/diag/log_file?name=stray_oca_soak (131 rows): 6 acted rows; 5 cancelled bare-numeric groups whose member perm ids are group+1/+2 (e.g. group 1502161095 -> perm 1502161096/97; 512599188 -> 512599189/90), i.e. native entry brackets, including 2026-09-10T09:43Z MGC with sibling keyed group oca-protect-t5573 open. The sweep (_sweep_stray_oca_groups, ib_client.py:3308) never reads parent_id. Module docstring/env-vars row claim sibling groups are 'self-identifying and preserved by construction'.
expected: A non-keyed group is cancelled only when it can be tied to the re-arming trade (e.g. parent permId/orderId = that trade's entry order).
actual: Any non-keyed group is cancelled; cannot tell own vs sibling.
population: Pure function crafted input (n=1); live soak n=131 rows, 6 acted, 5 on native-bracket groups; whether any of the 5 belonged to a sibling is NOT settled.
detector: Test: a numeric group whose parent_id is not the re-arming trade's entry order is preserved.
proposed_fix: Carry parentId in the sweep's leg read; cancel a non-keyed group only if its parentId matches the trade's journaled entry order id, else report as 'unkeyed_unowned'.
disposition: filed (paper-only today: allowlist is ib_paper, ib_live dry_run; pipeline item not required at medium)

claim: The protection re-assert attempt budget is keyed (account, symbol), counts SUCCESSFUL re-asserts, and is never reset, so after 3 re-asserts on one symbol in a process lifetime every later divergence on that symbol (any trade) is suppressed_attempts until restart.
evidence: grep -n _REASSERT_STATE src/runtime/*.py -> only order_monitor.py:8330 (decl), :8358 (read), :8407 (write attempts+1 on every will_act). No clear on success or on trade change. protection_reassert.py docstring: budget is for 'A re-assert that keeps failing'.
expected: Budget per trade (or reset on applied_state both_legs_resting / on divergence clearing).
actual: Per (account,symbol) for the process lifetime, successes included.
detector: Test: three successful re-asserts followed by a new divergence on a different trade id still yields reassert.
proposed_fix: Key _REASSERT_STATE by (account, symbol, trade_id) and reset attempts when applied_state == both_legs_resting.
disposition: filed (call site is in order_monitor.py, CA-A01's scope; recorded here as the module contract it breaks)

claim: run_package_leg_check never clears a latched gap whose package no longer has open legs, so /api/diag package_leg_coverage and package_leg_gaps() report closed packages as live exit-path gaps.
evidence: Crafted temp DB: run1 verdict stranded, gaps ['P1']; after closing the trade run2 packages assessed 0, gaps still latched: ['P1'] (src/runtime/package_leg_coverage.py loop only pops ids present in verdicts). LIVE: diag log_file?name=package_leg_coverage -> 25 latched packages; cross-checked against journal?table=trades (offsets 0/400/1400, ids 3826-6225): of the 35 legs named, 31 closed / 4 open; 21 of 25 packages have ALL legs closed (e.g. pkg-e6eac664c2a446a6 trade 4135 closed, latched since 2026-08-18).
expected: A package absent from the open-trade verdicts is un-latched.
population: Live latch file n=25 packages / 35 legs, 2026-09-27T13:14Z.
detector: Test: latch cleared after the package's last open leg closes.
proposed_fix: After assess(), drop every state key not in verdicts (except __last_check__).
